texts: How do I look for an iTaoBuy listing when I only have a photo?

Use the camera entry to open image search and crop the picture to one item. Examine several candidates. Compare seams, fasteners, labels and the original seller link before calling a result the same model.
Why might several sellers match the same reference photo?
Sellers can use similar studio shots or show visually close products. Compare the marketplace identifier, seller and selected version. The nearest image match gives you a candidate to investigate.
What do I keep when a spreadsheet link opens on iTaoBuy?
Save the original marketplace URL, seller's item number, selected option wording and quantity. The agent page and marketplace page serve different purposes, so keep a copy of both.
How do I compare two translated style labels that look identical?

Read each original label and keep any suffix, model number or swatch position. Select each option in turn and note which image, price or size range changes. Ask for clarification before choosing if the distinction remains unclear.
Can an item link preserve the colour I selected?
Test it by reopening the copied link and comparing the selection. If it returns to a default option, save the original option text and screenshot of the intended colour beside the link.
What should a manual note say for a two-tone colourway?
Give both colours, their positions on the item and the seller's option text or code. For example, distinguish a black body with white sleeves from a white body with black sleeves.
How do I tell whether a size chart gives flat width or circumference?

Look at the diagram and its endpoints. If the chart measures straight across a laid-flat garment, take the same flat measurement from one you own. Ask the seller when a heading gives only a number without a method.
When should I use a garment measurement instead of a body measurement?

Follow the chart definition. Compare a garment chart with a similar garment measured the same way. A body-size chart describes the wearer and may already allow for ease, so it requires a different comparison.
How do I verify what is included in a matching set?

Read the selected unit description, especially when separate pieces and complete sets share a listing. Keep the selection and subtotal together. The model's outfit in a promotional picture is insufficient evidence of quantity.
How can I separate QC photos for several nearly identical orders?
Use one folder or note per order line with the original option and warehouse reference. Keep at least one full view with the label close-up so the detail can be connected to that unit.
Can I use another buyer's QC measurement for my own order?
Use it as a reference only when the listing, size and measurement method are identifiable. To decide about your received unit, use a picture or measurement tied to its warehouse entry.
Why does a seller tracking number say delivered before I receive anything?

Check the destination of that shipment. Domestic delivery to the warehouse and an international parcel sent to you have different endpoints. Find the outbound parcel reference before looking for the final delivery scan.
How do I compare a CNY listing and a converted display price?

Record the underlying seller amount, option and quantity. Note the exchange rate and time of comparison, then verify the currency and total at checkout. Payment conversion and a catalogue display may produce different totals.
What should I include when reporting a parcel problem?
List the outbound parcel number, affected purchase reference, last known scan and a short description of the missing or damaged contents. Keep pictures of the label and packing with that record.
What can I do if a cropped image search finds the wrong item?

Try one crop that shows the outline and another that shows a distinctive construction detail. Remove unrelated garments and background logos. Open the best candidates and verify the option in the seller listing.
Should I confirm a replacement from a thumbnail alone?

Ask for the replacement's marketplace link and exact option text, then check the differences in material, size or quantity. Keep your approval associated with that version so your warehouse checks use the correct reference.
Where does iTaoBuy describe its ordering and QC service?

The developer's app listing explains link-based purchasing, warehouse photos and international shipping choices. For a question about a particular purchase or parcel, use the corresponding record in your account and its current support options.
Before opening an iTaoBuy spreadsheet link: check the listing, option and handoff

A spreadsheet row can be a convenient way to find a product, yet it condenses several decisions into one link. Follow the handoff from the catalogue to the seller and the agent before approving the actual purchase.
iTaoBuy · Google Play
iTaoBuy · App Store
Assign a job to each page

The spreadsheet is useful for discovery. The original marketplace page identifies what a particular seller is offering. The iTaoBuy purchase page records the selection you are preparing to submit through the agent. You might see the same title or photograph on all three, but this does not make them interchangeable. A catalogue price can be a starting price, an option on the seller page can be sold out and the import can default to another available choice. Review the final purchase record separately.

Suppose a row shows a dark overshirt with two chest pockets. You want that exact style in medium. The row tells you enough to open a candidate. It cannot, by itself, establish that the seller still offers the same construction in medium at the displayed amount. Write down the listing feature that made the row worth opening. Doing this at the start helps prevent a visually similar substitute from becoming your choice simply because it was the easiest option available on the next page.
Check the destination before entering account information

Look at the address of the actual page that opens. A button label can describe its intended destination, but the browser address tells you where you are. If you expected an agent purchase page and land on a different merchant, link-shortening service or an unexpected sign-in form, pause and identify why. A link opening a seller page for reference serves a different purpose from a link taking you to an agent checkout. Make sure the destination matches the action you intend to take.

For a saved marketplace listing, keep its original address and item identifier. If the agent link stops importing correctly, the developer's iTaoBuy app listing describes pasting marketplace links to start a purchase. Use the item reference to compare what the import returns. Avoid carrying unrelated tracking parameters into your notes when a clear marketplace item identifier is already available. At the same time, retain any genuinely necessary option information separately, since a product identifier often identifies a whole listing containing multiple styles.
Match the seller listing at more than one point

Compare the seller or shop name where visible, the marketplace item number and the option selector. Product titles are weak identifiers because translations can vary and sellers can reuse similar wording. Images can be shared across multiple offers. An identifier on a particular marketplace is stronger evidence of listing identity, but even a confirmed listing can change its contents over time. Check that the intended option still exists on the current page rather than relying exclusively on an old screenshot.

In the overshirt example, count the pockets and inspect the arrangement of the buttons. Then locate the dark option and see whether medium is available for that option. If neutral and dark versions have different constructions, select each to determine which specifications apply. A screenshot showing the dark cover photograph and a separate dropdown listing medium does not prove that dark medium is a valid combination. Try selecting the combination and read what the page actually displays for it.
Read the unit, quantity and price after selection

Ask what one unit buys. A listing for a shirt might include a separate accessory sold at a lower price. A set may offer the top, trousers and complete outfit under one title. A displayed range can include all of these options. Select the exact combination first and record the resulting unit price. Then set quantity and check the subtotal. Compare the seller's order unit with the quantity shown on iTaoBuy after import. A quantity of two might mean two garments or two sets.

Use a simple hypothetical example. A row starts at 38 yuan, a listing offers a separate belt at 38 and the overshirt at 118. Choosing two overshirts gives a merchandise subtotal of 236 yuan before other applicable charges. If you compare that with twice the headline number, the difference is an option difference, not necessarily a price error. Write the original currency alongside the amount. If the checkout also displays a conversion, retain the unconverted subtotal for comparison when the display currency changes.
Inspect what survives when the page is reopened

A saved link can reopen at the top of a product rather than the particular selection you had highlighted. Test this before sharing the link with a friend or handing it to another person preparing the order. Open the saved address in another tab, note the default selection and compare it with your record. If the choice resets, send the item link together with the original option text, colour and size. Add a screenshot showing the selector in context if the wording is ambiguous.

This matters even when the seller item number matches perfectly. Consider two versions described as dark blue and blue-black by one translation but both shown as navy by another. Record the original wording and the feature that distinguishes them, such as buttons, wash or pocket shape. A message that identifies the marketplace listing and intended selection gives the agent something actionable to check. A message containing only a photograph requires someone else to guess which option the seller meant.
Resolve the first disagreement before proceeding

When catalogue, seller and agent disagree, identify the first step at which the information changes. If the seller page no longer contains medium, the original row may be stale. If medium exists on the seller page but the agent import omits it, the question concerns the import or manual ordering route. If both list medium but the checkout subtotal changes after quantity is set, investigate unit pricing or domestic shipping. Different disagreements call for different evidence and different questions.

Send the smallest useful packet: original marketplace URL, item identifier, the option text you selected and one screenshot of the mismatch. Describe the outcome you want. For example, ask whether the dark-medium overshirt can be obtained at the selected unit price before purchase. Avoid authorizing a substitute merely by asking about availability. If you would accept another colour, specify which colour and any price limit in a separate instruction after you have seen the alternative listing.
Preserve a purchase record that can guide later QC

Once you choose to proceed, keep the row as a discovery reference and the final order as the authoritative record of your selection. Save the option, quantity, currency, amount and item reference from the purchase confirmation. When warehouse photographs become available, compare the received unit with this record. Start with the feature that originally mattered, then check label and quantity. Historical catalogue pictures can still help with comparison, but they do not replace photographs tied to your current purchase.

A good handoff ends with one concise statement: which seller listing you opened, which exact option you chose and which evidence remains to be checked after receipt. It can also end with a deliberate decision to leave a listing alone because the option or destination remains unclear. Either outcome is preferable to treating an attractive spreadsheet row as proof of current price, stock and identity all at once. The point of checking the link is to establish a purchase decision that another person can reproduce.

Check links again when returning to a saved spreadsheet weeks later. A marketplace listing can keep the same address after a seller changes the available options or removes the cheapest variant. Open your saved option record beside the current seller page. If the product code matches but the selected size has disappeared, the link still identifies a relevant listing while failing to provide a purchasable version of your original choice.
Does an iTaoBuy set include both pieces? Check the order unit before purchase

A listing can show a full outfit while selling the jacket, trousers and complete set under different options. Verify the selected unit, then preserve enough information to count what reaches the warehouse.
Read the listing as a set of offers

A hero photograph tells a visual story. A model may wear a jacket, trousers, belt and cap to show how they look together. The photograph alone says nothing definitive about which pieces the selected price buys. Open the seller options through the marketplace link and inspect the individual offers. Some listings use one selector for colour and another for product type. Others combine model, colour, size and unit into a single long string. Find the wording that identifies exactly what one ordered unit contains.

Imagine a dark tracksuit shown with a matching top and bottom. The first seller option is jacket only, the second trousers only and the third set. The catalogue card may display the first available price, which in this example could belong to the trousers. If you want the complete outfit, select the set and check both the resulting dollar or yuan amount and the available sizes. A larger price after switching selections can reflect a different number of pieces rather than a pricing discrepancy.
Separate component count from order quantity

Write two columns in your notes: units ordered and pieces per unit. One set containing a jacket and trousers is one order unit but two physical garments. Two such sets are two units and four garments. If the seller instead sells the jacket and trousers separately, one jacket plus one pair of trousers might appear as two order lines while yielding the same two garments. This distinction prevents both under-ordering and double counting when you review a later receipt.

Work through a hypothetical basket. A jacket costs 80 yuan, trousers 60 and the complete set 130. Ordering one jacket and one pair of trousers costs 140 before other charges, while selecting one complete set costs 130. Entering quantity two on the complete set would cost 260 and produce four garments if the offer is fulfilled as described. These invented values illustrate the method. Always read the actual seller unit, selected price and domestic charges before making the same comparison on a real listing.
Check whether top and bottom sizes can differ

A buyer might need a medium jacket and large trousers. Look at whether the complete-set selector allows independent sizes for each piece. A single size for the set may mean both pieces use that size, while separate individual options may give you more control. Do not assume a free-text note will override a fixed bundle. Ask whether the seller can supply your requested size mix and at what price before treating the mixed set as an available offer.

If the seller allows the mix, save the reply with the exact jacket and trouser sizes named. If the seller requires separate purchases, check both item identifiers and the resulting subtotal. If one piece is unavailable, decide whether the remaining item is acceptable on its own. An order note can state that you want to be contacted before buying an incomplete set. That instruction is more precise than asking the agent to “send whatever is available” when your original intent was to wear matching pieces together.
Distinguish styling props from included accessories

A cap, belt, detachable strap or small pouch can be included with one version and used as a styling prop in another. Look for a contents description, package list or seller message connected to the selected option. Compare the close photographs and see whether an accessory appears in multiple colours or only in a styled scene. Appearance in many pictures still does not establish inclusion if the purchase description says otherwise. Ask about the named piece directly where it affects your decision.

Use location and function to identify ambiguous accessories. For a bag, “small removable pouch attached to the inside ring” is clearer than “extra bag.” For a tracksuit, specify whether a waist belt is a separate accessory or a built-in drawstring. Save the seller's original wording before translating it for your own notes. If you receive an answer, preserve the question as well so that a short affirmative response is connected to the correct component and product option.
Verify the offer again on the agent purchase page

The iTaoBuy developer's description explains that the service reads pasted marketplace links. When the product opens, check that the intended set option has carried across and that quantity still means sets. Imported labels may be shortened, translated differently or default to the first entry. Compare the seller item identifier, option text and image. If the imported page shows only a colour and size with no component information, review the original selector before authorizing the purchase.

Create a compact expected-contents record at checkout. For example: one complete dark set; jacket medium and trousers large as confirmed; two garments total; no cap; selected option code and seller reference saved. Add the actual price and currency. This list gives the warehouse check a definite target. It also avoids confusing an agent-facing purchase confirmation that says “quantity one” with evidence that only a single physical garment should arrive.
Count what arrives using both evidence and context

Open the warehouse entry attached to the actual purchase and compare its photographs with your expected-contents list. A folded pair of trousers can be partly hidden beneath a jacket. A top-down photo of a sealed retail bag may show only the upper piece. An absent piece in a single photo is a reason to ask for a check, not proof it was never supplied. Request an overview showing both garments separately if quantity is important to your decision.

For several sets, request identification by order line or size combination. Four garments laid out together can establish overall count while leaving it unclear which jacket belongs with which trousers. If the seller ships pieces separately, retain each domestic tracking reference and check for an outstanding second package. Do not submit the first piece internationally simply because its warehouse entry is visible if you intend to inspect and ship the complete set together.
Resolve discrepancies before changing the packing

If the warehouse confirms a missing piece, provide the seller option description, purchase confirmation and expected-contents record. Name the absent component and ask what information is available about split dispatch or seller fulfilment. If the complete set arrived but one size is wrong, identify exactly which piece and whether the other one matches the accepted mix. This distinction helps support ask for the appropriate remedy rather than returning an entire set before the seller confirms what it needs.

Before disposing of packaging or separating components, check any return or exchange requirements relevant to that order. If the seller offers a partial resolution, compare it with your actual need. A partial credit may still leave you with an unusable half-outfit, while a replacement piece from another batch may differ in shade. Record the accepted outcome and recheck the eventual contents. The final picture you want is a complete match between the selected offer, the quantity paid for and the pieces you can identify in the warehouse.

Some listings include a case as packaging while others sell it as a separate component. The distinction matters when a group splits a purchase. Two brushes inside one fitted case may reasonably be described as a two-piece brush set, even though three objects arrive. Ask what each person expects to take home, then match that expectation to the seller's itemized contents. If both people need separate cases, record that requirement before ordering, since seeing one case in a picture cannot establish that each brush gets its own.
iTaoBuy price comparison: convert a seller price without losing sight of checkout

A price in yuan, a catalogue conversion and a card charge can all describe the same purchase at different stages. Put the figures on a common basis before deciding that a listing costs more or less than another.
Write down the item behind the number

Before opening a calculator, identify the marketplace listing, the selected option and the unit being sold. A product page may show a low starting amount for an accessory beside a photograph of the complete item. Another listing may show the price of a pair or a bundle. Changing the currency cannot make these units comparable. Select the option you would actually purchase, set a realistic quantity and capture its subtotal with the original currency still visible.

Suppose a listing offers a single cover, a pair of covers and a cushion with an insert. You want two covers. If the initial number describes one cover, multiply the correct single-unit selection by two unless the seller offers a separate pair option. If the pair has an explicit price, compare that with the single-unit alternative. Keep the unit description as a column in the comparison. A note that says only “row A: 79, row B: 88” leaves the most important assumption completely hidden.
Choose a rate direction and keep the units visible

An exchange rate can be written as yuan per unit of your currency or units of your currency per yuan. Those descriptions are reciprocals. Write the direction in plain words before calculating. For a purely illustrative rate of eight yuan per unit of another currency, an 80-yuan item equals ten units before additional charges. Divide by eight to convert yuan into that currency. Multiplying by eight instead produces a number with no meaningful relationship to the intended conversion.

If your rate is written the other way round, such as 0.125 units per yuan in this imaginary example, multiply 80 by 0.125 to arrive at ten. Check the two methods on a convenient amount before trusting a spreadsheet column. A simple diagnostic is to convert the result back using the same rate. Ten times eight returns 80 yuan. Small differences from rounding are normal; a result that is several times larger than the starting value calls for a check of the formula and units.
Separate the item subtotal from seller-to-warehouse delivery

Now consider a fictional seller offering two covers at 42 yuan each and charging six yuan to send the combined purchase to the warehouse. The item subtotal is 84 yuan; the domestic purchase total is 90 yuan. At the made-up rate of eight yuan per currency unit, those are 10.50 and 11.25 respectively. Both converted numbers can be correct, but they describe different scopes. Label the first “goods” and the second “goods plus domestic delivery” in your notes.

If another seller quotes 88 yuan for a pair including domestic delivery, compare 88 with 90 rather than 84. At this stage the second seller is two yuan cheaper under the stated conditions. You still need to compare what the two products include, seller terms and the final purchase page. Do not attach the entire price of a later international shipment to one of the listings unless it is the only item in that parcel and the assumptions match on both sides.
Know what the currency selector can answer

The currency control on a catalogue helps you browse in familiar numbers. It is especially useful when comparing several shortlist entries in one sitting under the same rate assumptions. Record the displayed original price where possible, the selected currency and the time of your comparison. A different display tomorrow could reflect a rate update, a changed item option or a seller price revision. Keeping the original amount lets you test those explanations separately instead of assuming the item itself became more expensive.

At checkout read the currency code beside the final amount. A symbol alone can be ambiguous. Record which party is presenting the price and whether the payment screen offers another conversion. A catalogue is not the processor of the later transaction. The developer's iTaoBuy listing describes link-based purchases and international payment choices; the account's actual payment screen supplies the applicable details for your purchase. Use that screen for the specific amount you are about to authorize and save its transaction reference.
Test an apparent price difference with a controlled example

Imagine that two screenshots show 12.00 and 12.80 in your preferred currency. You cannot conclude that the second has a worse exchange rate from those figures alone. First inspect the seller price on both. If the first includes 96 yuan of goods and the second includes the same goods plus eight yuan of domestic postage, the higher amount can result from scope even when both use an identical rate. Recalculate from the original components before comparing the conversions themselves.

Next hold the original subtotal constant. With a 96-yuan purchase converted to 12 units, the implied rate is eight yuan per unit. The same 96 yuan converted to 12.80 implies 7.5 yuan per unit, provided no additional amount is bundled into either figure. That proviso is important. An apparent implied rate can absorb a service or payment charge if the screen combines entries. Call it a comparison of effective totals until the checkout explicitly identifies how the amounts are calculated.
Reconcile a settled payment without counting conversion twice

For a completed purchase, save the seller or agent receipt, payment confirmation and posted account amount. Use the identifiers to ensure they concern the same purchase. A pending authorization may later change or disappear; match a settled entry when reconciling final cost. Remove personal account details from screenshots you share with support and show only the currency, amount, relevant reference and date. A long statement containing unrelated transactions rarely helps someone answer a question about a single order.

Build a short sequence from the original item to the posted amount. Start with goods and domestic delivery in their original currency. Add only charges explicitly recorded. Note the payment currency and amount next. If the bank records a further conversion, put that in a separate column. Avoid applying your own model rate again to an amount already denominated in your account currency. That common mistake can make a completely ordinary purchase look dramatically different from the amount you actually paid.
Decide whether a small difference should change the purchase

After normalizing unit, scope, currency and time, ask what remains material to your decision. A tiny conversion difference may be less important than a seller option that includes both pieces you need, an identified size chart or clearer product evidence. If the remaining gap is large, return to the payment screen and look for the first stage at which the totals diverge. A focused question identifying a particular subtotal is much easier to resolve than a general complaint about conversion.

Keep the final comparison reproducible. One good row says which listing and option you chose, how many units, the original subtotal, domestic delivery, checkout currency and amount, and which rate was merely illustrative. When international freight is quoted later, enter it as a new transaction for the actual parcel. This preserves the difference between comparing products before purchase and calculating the overall cost once packaging and transport are known. It also lets you reuse the same method when shopping in a different display currency.

For a shared purchase, agree on the currency used to divide the bill and keep evidence of the actual amount charged. Dividing the cart's rounded display price may leave a small discrepancy once the transaction posts. A fair record shows the original checkout amount, the settled total and the number of items allocated to each person. Label any later international freight separately so the group can see what changed.
iTaoBuy tracking: keep seller delivery, warehouse intake and international dispatch separate

A “delivered” scan can mean that a seller's box reached a warehouse in China while your international parcel has yet to be created. Follow the references through each stage instead of asking one tracking number to describe the whole journey.
Start by naming both ends of the journey

Identify the sender and intended recipient for the tracking event you are reading. The seller-to-warehouse journey has the seller at one end and the receiving warehouse at the other. The warehouse-to-you journey begins later, once an outbound parcel exists. The same purchase can appear in both journeys under different references. A domestic delivery event tells you something about the movement of the seller's package. It does not establish the delivery date of a future international parcel.

Consider two shirts from different sellers. One seller dispatches on Monday and the domestic carrier records delivery to a warehouse on Wednesday. The other seller has not dispatched. You intend to send both shirts together internationally. The Wednesday event cannot possibly confirm delivery of the combined parcel, because at that point the second shirt has not reached the warehouse. Drawing the endpoints of the current shipment is often enough to explain what initially looks like a contradictory or alarming tracking update.
Keep the purchase line and the domestic package distinct

Save the purchase reference, seller listing, selected options and quantity for each order. Then attach any domestic carrier reference supplied for that purchase. A seller can split a purchase across more than one package, or put several pieces in one. Consequently a one-to-one table between item and tracking number may break down. Allow several item references to share a domestic number and allow a single purchase to have more than one domestic number where the seller's records support it.

For an order containing a shirt and matching trousers, record which pieces the seller says were placed in each box. If the seller has supplied two numbers but no allocation, mark the allocation unknown. Do not infer that the first number belongs to the shirt because the shirt was listed first. When the warehouse records the incoming contents, use that evidence to complete the mapping. This small distinction prevents a genuinely outstanding box from being misreported as a missing component in a box that never contained it.
Read warehouse intake as its own event

A carrier scan describes a logistics event. Warehouse intake identifies goods within the receiving system. A delivery scan and an item appearing in warehouse inventory therefore supply different pieces of evidence. If one appears without the other, check the domestic number, warehouse destination and purchase reference. Record the time of the last confirmed event using the time zone shown. Avoid extrapolating a guaranteed intake interval from another buyer's order or from an unrelated carrier's display.

The developer describes iTaoBuy as purchasing and shipping on request and supplying QC photos after the seller sends goods to the warehouse. For an individual purchase, look for the warehouse entry or photographs connected to your order. A product photo attached to the right entry can help confirm which unit arrived. A generic seller photograph or historical QC reference cannot do that job. If you need support, send the domestic reference, purchase identifier and which received item is missing from the account record.
Connect warehouse entries to the outbound parcel

When you choose the items to send internationally, save a list of their warehouse entries beside the new parcel reference. Several seller packages can contribute to one outbound parcel; one warehouse entry may also be left behind for another shipment. Identify what is actually included rather than treating everything in storage as dispatched. This becomes particularly important when one item is under inspection or waiting for an exchange and the remainder are ready to travel.

For the two shirts, suppose the first shirt is accepted and the second is awaiting a size check. If you decide to ship only the first, record that choice explicitly. The international tracking page for the first parcel cannot tell you when the second shirt will leave. Conversely, if you decide to wait and consolidate, there may be no outbound tracking number yet. In both cases the explanation comes from the parcel contents and submission decision, not from the domestic carrier's earlier delivery scan.
Distinguish a label from movement and movement from delivery

Read the wording of each outbound event carefully. A reference or label can exist before the carrier has recorded a physical handoff. A transit event can show movement through part of the route without establishing a delivery appointment. A local-carrier number, if one is provided, may describe a later stage of the same international parcel. Record the carrier and reference together rather than overwriting the original outbound number when a second identifier appears.

If the same event appears on two tracking pages with slightly different labels, compare the event time, location and parcel reference. A translation can turn an operational status into an overly definite-sounding statement. When the scope remains uncertain, quote the actual event text in your support message and ask what stage it represents. Resist filling gaps with a guessed customs decision, exact flight or delivery date. An absence of new public scans gives much less information than a confirmed exception from the responsible carrier.
Investigate one missing link at a time

Start with the last event you can independently associate with the correct shipment. If there is no domestic number and the seller order still shows no dispatch, the inquiry belongs with purchase status. If a domestic number shows warehouse delivery but no purchase line is matched, the question concerns intake. If the warehouse entry is present but no parcel includes it, review parcel submission. If a submitted international parcel has a carrier reference but an unresolved exception, use the outbound record and carrier information.

Write a message that identifies the gap. For example: “Seller package A is marked delivered to the warehouse on the domestic carrier page. The account shows the matching shirt order but I cannot find its warehouse entry. Can you check whether it has been matched?” This is more actionable than “Where is my parcel?” because the reader knows which journey and which handoff need attention. Include only the personal or shipment information needed through the platform's private support channel.
Verify delivery against physical contents

When the outbound parcel arrives, retain the label and compare its reference with your saved parcel record. Check the contents against the warehouse entries that were selected for this shipment, including any item intentionally left out. If something is missing, distinguish a piece absent from an included set from a whole item that was never selected. Keep relevant packaging and photographs while checking the platform's current reporting procedure. An item's domestic delivery record cannot settle a discrepancy in the outbound contents by itself.

Close the tracking record with a simple chain of references linking seller purchase, domestic package, warehouse entry, outbound parcel and delivery. Leave unresolved links clearly marked. This gives you a reusable way to understand combined and split orders without assuming that every stage uses the same number. More importantly, it lets you ask the right party a precise question about the last confirmed handoff and the next event you actually need to verify.

For a delivery involving a collection point, keep the notification naming that point alongside the carrier history. A scan indicating arrival at a pickup location creates a different practical task from a scan confirming collection. Check the address and collection instructions through the carrier's own channel before travelling. If a person other than the intended recipient collected the parcel, record the evidence the carrier provides and contact the relevant support channel with the destination tracking number and observed discrepancy.
Save the final collection receipt alongside the corresponding tracking record.
How to find the original iTaoBuy listing from a product photo

An image match can bring a promising listing to the top while hiding a different seller, option or size range. Use image search to build a shortlist, then identify which result contains enough evidence for the purchase you have in mind.
Decide what “the same item” means in this search

You see a photograph of a cream canvas bag with a dark base and want to find the listing behind it. There are at least three worthwhile outcomes. You might recover the exact link the photographer used. You might find a seller offering an apparently identical model under another listing. Or you might find a similar bag that meets your needs. Decide which outcome matters before spending time on the search. If the original poster provided a marketplace URL, start with it. A visual lookup is most useful when that direct route is missing.

Describe two or three details in words while the original picture is in front of you. For this example, there might be a curved seam at the base, a front pocket with a diagonal opening and a strap attached to a metal ring. These details let you compare candidates after a new image or similar product name has drawn your attention. If your only description is “cream tote bag,” almost any plausible result can feel like a match. A short list of visible details gives you a more demanding test.
Prepare a crop for shape and a crop for construction

Begin with the outline. Remove surrounding people, captions, account names, collages and objects occupying more of the frame than the product. Leave the complete bag in view, including its handles and base. A tight crop of a graphic or zipper may suppress exactly the silhouette that distinguishes the product. Use the camera entry on this site's search interface and submit the crop. Keep the original untouched so that you can return to omitted details later.

For a second query, crop around a structural feature that the first picture does not emphasize. A pocket plus its surrounding seam gives more context than a close-up of a common metal buckle. Change just this part of the search first. When you change the crop, lighting, orientation and background in a single edit, you cannot tell which change altered the matches. Compare the shortlists and mark candidates appearing in both. Frequency across searches can justify opening a result, but it does not establish where the original photograph was taken.
Separate seller catalogues from the photograph trail

Open promising product pages and find the source marketplace link if it is available. Record the marketplace and the listing identifier, together with the shop name you see on the seller page. An agent-facing URL can provide another view of the same seller listing. A different seller can also display the same image under an entirely different item number. Make a separate record whenever marketplace or listing identity changes, even if the gallery looks familiar.

Imagine results A and B have identical studio photos, while C has a less polished picture showing the diagonal pocket and ring attachment. A and B could be showing a photograph shared through a supply chain. C might help answer what the item looks like under different conditions, but a rougher picture does not prove that C supplied the original. Look for a link or attribution from the original post, a matching item number, an order reference you control or another reliable connection. Until then, describe them as visual candidates.
Test the variant rather than accepting the hero photograph

On each shortlisted listing, open the option selector and choose the colour shown in the original. Observe which elements change. The lead image may change to a swatch, the displayed price may change, or the same photograph may remain for the whole listing. If more than one option could match, save the original option text and compare any accompanying description. Two bags called ivory in translation might differ by size, strap style or whether the darker base is included.

For the cream bag, a result that shows the correct pocket but offers only an all-cream base is a partial match. A result with three base colours but no image attached to the chosen option leaves an unresolved question. In either case, identify the single detail that separates the candidates. Asking whether the charcoal-bottom version is available with the diagonal pocket is easier to answer than sending a collage and asking a seller, “Is it the same?” A catalogue hit becomes useful when it narrows the question.
Use measurements to reject plausible lookalikes

Pictures rarely reveal scale cleanly. A small handbag and a larger tote can share handle proportions, stitching and studio styling. Look for dimensions tied to the chosen option, including the unit and the points being measured. A width measured at the open top of a tapered bag differs from its base width. If you need the bag to hold a particular object, measure that object first and allow for the opening and closure rather than relying on the external width alone.

Consider a hypothetical notebook 29 centimetres long. A seller's stated exterior width of 30 centimetres does not tell you whether the notebook will pass through a zipped opening shorter than the body. A straight-on picture that makes the notebook appear small also gives no reliable clearance measurement. Ask about the opening or compare an object of known dimensions in an image where perspective is controlled. This second check can eliminate a mistaken size even when the visual model is otherwise correct.
Carry the evidence into the iTaoBuy order

The developer's iTaoBuy app description explains that buyers can paste marketplace links and use warehouse photographs to review items. Once you reach a candidate you want to order, paste the seller link into the agent and check that the imported page shows the intended option. Compare the price after selection, the quantity, the source listing and any seller-specific notes. If the agent page resets the selection, apply it again and record the final state before approving the purchase.

Keep the picture trail compact. Save the original reference; one screenshot of the chosen seller listing and its selected option; and your short list of unresolved checks. For our bag that list might be “dark base, diagonal pocket, opening wide enough for notebook.” When the warehouse entry becomes available, evaluate that unit against the list. The photograph that launched the search remains a reference image. The warehouse photographs attached to the actual purchase now carry more weight for deciding whether to ship the unit you received.
Know when the exact original remains unknown

Sometimes several shops show the same photographs and none supplies an identifier connecting it to the original post. Write down what you can establish: same visible design, similar measurements, or matching option description. Leave seller identity unknown if you cannot connect the records. This makes the buying decision more honest and more useful. You can still compare price and terms between candidates without turning a visual resemblance into an unsupported claim about origin.

If the distinctive feature is decisive and no listing shows it clearly, the efficient next step is one specific request for evidence, not a longer list of increasingly similar pictures. If the feature is optional and several alternatives meet your needs, compare them on their own terms. Close your search with the seller link, selected option and the reason for choosing it. Those three things will outlast a numbered position in search results and will still make sense when you review the warehouse photographs days later.

A cropped image can hide the one feature that distinguishes two otherwise identical models. If the original photo is available, inspect the uncropped edges for a clasp, pocket opening or printed code. Record how that feature appears on each candidate listing before committing to one.
Organizing iTaoBuy QC photos when several similar items arrive together

Three nearly identical shirts can produce a gallery full of convincing pictures without proving which size belongs to which order. Build an item-by-item record that ties each photograph to the decision it actually supports.
Use the warehouse entry as the organizing unit

Start with the order lines and warehouse entries visible in your account. Give each received unit or clearly identified group a separate row. Record the purchase reference, seller option, expected quantity and warehouse reference. If a single order includes several identical units, label their individual identities as unknown unless the warehouse records actually distinguish them. A neat filing system is useful only if it preserves the limits of what you know. Numbering a photograph “unit three” cannot make it evidence about a third unit.

Imagine that you ordered two blue shirts in medium and a blue shirt in large. A front view of a blue shirt confirms something about colour and design but little about size or count. Make three expected-unit rows, then attach photographs only where the account record supports the connection. If the warehouse supplies one shared gallery for a group, keep it at group level until you can identify the pieces. This prevents a single attractive photograph from being counted as a separate check for all three clothes.
Keep original and annotated pictures apart

Save or reference the original photograph with its warehouse entry. When you crop or draw an arrow, retain the original and label the copy by purpose, such as “medium tag enlarged” or “stitch near right cuff.” Cropping can be excellent for showing a small detail, yet it can remove the surroundings that associate the detail with the actual garment. Put a full-unit overview beside the close-up. If both images come from a sequence, keep their original order or note their source.

Avoid depending entirely on a phone's date sorting. Images can be downloaded on a different day from when the warehouse took them, or several orders can be downloaded together. Sorting by the download date might interleave an old reference photograph with new pictures. Include the purchase or warehouse reference in your folder or note. For sensitive account identifiers, keep the record private. If you share a picture publicly for a style opinion, remove unrelated order labels and personal details first.
Record which property each view can support

Write a short label for the question answered by each image. A front overview might establish the panel design. A complete size-tag photo may establish the attached label. A tape-measure image might establish width if both endpoints and units are shown. A seller studio photograph can be a comparison reference but cannot confirm the condition of your specific unit. Using these distinctions prevents a large photo count from creating false confidence about properties that no photograph actually addresses.

For the three shirts, check visible colour and pattern from the overviews, then inspect size evidence individually. A picture labelled medium and another labelled large can show two label values without proving there are two medium shirts. A third overview showing all three units together can help establish quantity. If labels still cannot be linked to distinct garments, record the uncertainty. The right response may be a single grouped photograph with the relevant labels visible, subject to what the warehouse can provide.
Use an expected-versus-observed table

Each row can contain expected item, observed evidence, unresolved question and next action. Keep the observation narrow. For example, “medium label visible on warehouse entry A” is stronger and more precise than “correct size and perfect fit.” Fit requires additional measurements or a physical try-on. Similarly, “front print appears centred in this image” is a more defensible statement than a broad quality verdict. The difference matters when another person later relies on the notes to approve international shipment.

Consider a case where medium shirt A matches the design, medium shirt B has no readable label and large shirt C has a clear label but the cuff is folded out of view. Two distinct evidence requests emerge. If size is crucial for B, ask for its attached label. If a cuff issue is suspected for C, ask to see that cuff unfolded. Do not ask for three new full galleries indiscriminately. Specific requests use the existing evidence and tell the warehouse exactly what remains unresolved.
Handle repeated photographs and near-duplicates

A cropped copy and its full original represent one observation of the same scene. A gallery can also contain several angles of a single unit. Do not count those as separate pieces merely because filenames or image URLs differ. Conversely, two similar shirts photographed against the same table can produce almost identical overviews even when the units really are distinct. Resolve identity with the warehouse entry, label and physical arrangement, rather than guessing from image similarity alone.

If you suspect a photograph belongs to the wrong entry, describe the conflict rather than accusing the warehouse of reusing an image. For example, one entry is for a blue medium but the visible label reads large, while the next entry is for a blue large. Ask whether the label picture was attached to the intended unit. Keep the earlier images while the check proceeds. If a corrected image arrives, record what it replaces so that the superseded picture does not accidentally guide a later decision.
Distinguish a previous buyer's QC from your own

A historical QC finder or catalogue gallery can be useful when researching a seller before purchase. Label such evidence as a reference and store it separately from the actual warehouse record. Match marketplace listing, option and date where possible. A previous buyer may have selected a different size, colour or production version. Even a highly relevant historical image cannot establish that your received garment has the same label or lacks the same visible defect.

The iTaoBuy developer describes supplying warehouse QC photos for buyers to review. When your own images appear, use the new order-linked evidence for the current unit and keep the historical image only for the specific comparison it supports. If historical photos show a stitched emblem and your received unit appears printed, compare clear close-ups tied to the exact variant before deciding the seller changed the product. It is also possible that the public reference came from a different option within the same listing.
Finish with a per-item release decision

Before sending the group internationally, mark each expected item separately as ready, awaiting evidence or requiring support. A correct blue large should not automatically clear two blue mediums, and one disputed item should not silently block another if you intended separate shipments. Compare the release list with the actual parcel contents. If items are repacked or warehouse entries consolidated, retain the mapping from old identifiers to the outbound parcel record so that the photographs remain meaningful after dispatch.

Keep the final archive small enough to use. For each item, retain its order confirmation, one identifying overview, the decisive detail and your conclusion. If something remains uncertain, state whether you accepted that uncertainty or requested another check. Later, when the package arrives, compare each piece against those records. You can then distinguish a pre-existing concern from an issue first observed after delivery and explain the difference without sifting through dozens of anonymous images of similar blue shirts.

Give the recipient a simple way to distinguish the final pieces. If the buyer chose two nearly identical shirts for different people, keep a private note mapping each warehouse reference to its intended recipient and verified size. A carrier label on the international carton will identify neither individual shirt. After delivery, the recipient can consult the assignment note and the same label photographs used at inspection without reopening the original conversation with the seller.
How to prepare an iTaoBuy parcel support request
Build a clear support request for an incomplete, delayed or damaged parcel using the correct order, shipment and evidence.
iTaoBuy
Start with the decision you need

A good support request tells the reader what happened, which transaction it affects and what answer would let you move forward. Start with one sentence you could read aloud. For example, “My international parcel arrived with two of the three storage pouches on the dispatch list. Can you confirm which package contained the green pouch?” This gives the agent an identifiable item and a question that they can check against the packing record.

Separate what you observed from any theory about the cause. You can count the two pouches on your desk. You may be able to identify an outer cut in the shipping bag. Unless someone documented the entire packing and delivery journey, you generally cannot know where a third pouch went missing. Describing the observed count and condition gives staff several ways to investigate. Accusing the seller or carrier in the first line can steer the discussion toward a stage of the journey that has yet to be identified.
Choose the right order and shipment identifiers

Keep the purchase number, warehouse reference and international parcel number in separate fields. A domestic tracking number relates to the journey from a seller to the receiving warehouse. An international parcel can contain items from several sellers. Copy each identifier directly from the appropriate record. Add the corresponding carrier when the same sequence of digits could belong to different tracking services. A clear label saves the next reader from having to guess which system holds the information.

If you ordered two similar products, describe the affected variant as well as the product. “Green roll-top pouch, medium, quantity one” is easier to match than “the bag.” Where the original order displays a seller style code, include it alongside your plain-language description. A warehouse label may use the code while the order page uses a translated name. Those two pieces of information allow the agent to follow the same item across records without needing to interpret a photograph of similar green products.
Give a short timeline with an end point

Write the events that materially changed the case. For a parcel received incomplete, this could include the warehouse check, international parcel submission, delivery and first count. Record the local date and add a time zone when comparing events from different countries. Leave out routine notifications that contribute no new fact. Four dated events and an accurate final observation can be easier to act on than a long transcript of every refresh of a tracking page.

A delayed parcel needs a different end point. Record the latest carrier event exactly enough to distinguish an electronic label announcement from physical receipt, and say when you last checked. If the destination carrier has assigned a separate number, provide that record as well. Ask which party can check the next movement and whether the platform needs any action from you. A generic estimate from another buyer's delivery cannot establish the status of your package or the date that a carrier considers it eligible for an investigation.
Select evidence for the particular problem

For missing contents, take one overview showing the received items laid out separately and a second image showing the dispatch contents record. Keep the outer wrapping and any inner packaging while the matter is open. For visible damage, capture the whole item and a closer view of the affected part. A small tear shown alone can be hard to orient. Including a wider shot gives the reviewer a way to locate it and compare it with earlier images.

For the pouch example, name the two received colours and show them beside each other. If all pouches were supposed to be nested, say whether you checked inside each one. An overview taken after that check can answer a question staff would otherwise need to send back. If opening a sealed retail package could affect a remedy you are considering, explain the limit of your inspection and ask for guidance. Document the current condition before making any change requested by the agent.
Keep private information within the case

A shipping label may contain a name, full street address, phone number and tracking code. Use the support entry point in your account or the contact information identified through the platform's own website or app listing. When sharing an example publicly, remove personal details and readable barcodes from the copy. Retain the original privately in case the authorized support contact requests a specific field for verification. A cropped copy lets you discuss a case without circulating the full delivery label.

Number the attachments and explain what each one shows. For example, the first image shows two pouches in different colours, the second shows the three-line dispatch record and the third shows the outside of the shipping bag at receipt. Say when each image was taken if that affects interpretation. An order screenshot taken after a partial refund might show a different quantity from the purchase confirmation. Supplying the date helps staff understand the apparent discrepancy before spending time investigating the wrong number.
Ask for a specific next action

Following the pouch example, a practical first request is for staff to compare the final packing entry against the warehouse record for the green item. If they confirm it was never included, ask which options apply and what each would involve. If the packing entry records all three, ask what evidence is needed to continue through the appropriate channel. Keep promises about compensation, replacement or freight out of your own summary unless someone has actually made them for your case.

For a damage case, explain the outcome you need in everyday terms. A cracked buckle might leave a bag unusable even though its fabric looks intact. Say whether you are asking about a replacement part or a remedy for the entire item. Include any seller or parcel protection information attached to the actual transaction. Ask for applicable reporting requirements while the evidence is available. Terms can differ by order and route, so save the response that refers specifically to your parcel.
Keep the next person up to date

Once the request has a reference number, use it for follow-up and keep the conversation in one place when possible. Add new information in a short update. “The destination carrier found a second package under this additional tracking number” immediately changes a missing-item investigation. Reposting the whole original message without calling out that new number makes it harder to see what changed. If a second channel must be used, include the earlier case reference and most recent answer.

Close the file only when the agreed action can be checked. A replacement being discussed, a replacement with a tracking number and a replacement received are three distinct stages. A refund offered and a credit actually visible in the designated account are also different events. Write a final sentence giving the original discrepancy, the verified result and the date. If a replacement green pouch arrived a week after the other two, the buyer and support agent can both see exactly how the order was completed.

If someone else accepted the delivery, identify which observations came from that person. For example, a housemate can confirm that the bag was left at reception, while you can confirm the contents you unpacked that evening. Ask the housemate to save any relevant delivery photograph. Attributing each detail to its observer keeps the account accurate when the carrier later asks who physically received the parcel and who first noticed the discrepancy.
Using an iTaoBuy size chart: compare a flat garment with the seller's measurements

A translated chart can say “chest 58” without telling you whether that number is a width, a circumference or a measurement of the wearer. Reconstruct the measurement method before using the figure to choose a size.
Choose a garment that answers the same fit question

Start with the intended use. If you want a sweatshirt to fit over a shirt, find a sweatshirt you already wear that way. A close-fitting T-shirt may have the same printed size but will be a poor reference for how much room you need. Zip or button comparable garments as you normally wear them and lay them flat without stretching. Smooth wrinkles that would distort a reading while preserving the natural shape. Write down which reference garment you used so that a second measurement can be reproduced.

Identify the fit problem you are trying to avoid. A sweatshirt can have enough chest room yet feel short when you raise your arms. A jacket can close comfortably yet pull across the upper back when you reach forward. Choose two or three measurements relevant to that problem. A single size code or overall impression is rarely enough. A record giving flat chest width, back length and sleeve method lets you compare seller charts without assuming that all brands build a garment to the same proportions.
Read the seller's diagram before translating the headings

Open the original listing linked to the exact style on iTaoBuy. Find the chart, diagram or image associated with that style, not a chart for another model shown elsewhere in the gallery. Translated headings are useful starting points, but diagrams can reveal where the measurement begins and ends. Look for units and whether the dimensions describe the garment itself or a recommended wearer. If the heading and diagram appear inconsistent, save both and ask which method the seller used.

For example, a line drawn from one underarm seam to the other across a flat garment describes a width. A circumference refers to the distance around the garment or wearer, depending on the chart. A seller might also describe a recommended body range, such as a range of chest measurements intended for a particular size. Doubling a flat garment width produces an approximate garment circumference under simple assumptions. It does not automatically create a recommended body measurement or account for stretch, lining and the ease built into the design.
Work through two charts that use different conventions

Suppose your comparison sweatshirt measures 57 centimetres from underarm to underarm laid flat. Listing A reports a flat chest width of 56 centimetres for one option and 59 for the next. Relative to your own garment, one is a centimetre narrower in flat width and the other is two centimetres wider. This arithmetic gives you a useful comparison only if the tape crosses the same points and neither garment is stretched. The decision about which difference you would prefer is personal.

Listing B gives 114 centimetres as the garment chest circumference for one option. If the seller confirms it represents twice the same flat width, it corresponds approximately to 57 centimetres, matching the reference sweatshirt on this one measure. If 114 is actually a recommended body measurement, that conclusion no longer follows. The examples are hypothetical and concern no particular seller. Their purpose is to show why a surprisingly close number is not a reason to skip verifying what the published number describes.
Measure length and sleeves without mixing starting points

Back length can be measured from the collar seam, from the high point of the shoulder or from another named point in a seller diagram. A ribbed collar or raised hood seam can add confusion if you start from its outer edge. Measure your reference sweatshirt using the seller's illustrated endpoints. If the garment tapers or has a curved hem, note whether the endpoint is at the centre back or side. A measurement to the shortest part of the hem cannot be fairly compared with one to the longest point.

Sleeves need similar care. A conventional shoulder seam gives a recognizable starting point. A dropped shoulder moves that seam down the arm. A raglan sleeve runs towards the neckline and may have no conventional shoulder seam at all. Two sleeves of equal measured length from their respective arm seams can therefore place the cuff differently on the wearer. Ask for neck-to-cuff or another shared method when the cuts differ. Write the method next to the number, even if the seller's chart labels both figures simply “sleeve.”
Compare uncertainties instead of chasing millimetres

A soft garment changes shape depending on how it is laid out. Ribbed fabric can stretch while the tape is being pulled into place. A folded seam can shorten a measurement by more than the difference between two nearly identical readings. Repeat your reference measurement once with the tape removed between attempts. If your own result changes noticeably, a tiny displayed difference in a chart deserves less confidence than a large difference confirmed by the same method.

Separate uncertainty about measurement from preference about fit. You may be certain that a jacket is four centimetres longer than your current one and still unsure whether you will like the extra length. Conversely, you may know exactly how much extra room you want but lack a reliable reading of the seller's width. In the first case, try comparing with another garment you own. In the second, seek a clearer chart or a measurement photograph before letting a promotional description make the decision for you.
Tie a later warehouse measurement to the unit you ordered

The iTaoBuy developer describes warehouse QC photos in its app listing. If a measurement is essential, check the current options for the individual order and ask a specific question. Name the purchase reference, colour and size. Describe how the garment should be positioned, the two points between which the tape should run and the unit to use. Ask for a picture wide enough to show both endpoints and the tape lying flat. A crisp close-up of the final number cannot establish where the measurement began.

Keep at least one image connecting the unit with the size label. This matters if several similar pieces arrived. Compare the warehouse result with your reference and chart using the same convention. If the label is correct but dimensions appear different, describe that discrepancy precisely: ordered medium, medium tag visible, measured back length from collar seam differs from the medium chart using the same endpoints. That gives support an observable question to investigate. Saying only “this looks small” leaves too many explanations open.
Make a decision you can reproduce later

Write a final comparison in ordinary language. It might read, “Option M is close to my sweatshirt across the chest, but the back is shorter by three centimetres using the same collar-to-hem method. Sleeve length remains uncertain because the designs use different seams.” This gives you a reason to order, ask for clarification or choose another listing. It also gives you a useful reference if the seller later edits the chart or another buyer's photograph circulates with an unclear size label.

For your next search, keep the reference garment and measurement notes rather than memorizing that a particular letter size once fit. Sizes can differ across sellers and options on the same platform. A small set of consistently measured garments is more transferable. When the original chart, selected option, relevant photographs and comparison notes all point to the same conclusion, you can make a much better-informed fit decision without pretending that a spreadsheet or a single image can predict exactly how a garment will feel.

Repeat the reference measurement after lifting and laying down the garment again. If the result changes substantially, describe that uncertainty and check the starting points before deciding between neighbouring sizes.
Reading translated iTaoBuy style labels without mixing up two options

Product selectors often compress material, colour, size and bundle details into a few words. Preserve the original option labels, isolate the difference between choices and carry the intended version through to your order.
Start with the selector, not the translated title

A listing title may combine every version a seller offers. The translated name can describe a whole family of jackets even when the actual choices include a short jacket, long jacket, lined version and unlined version. Open the listing and identify the controls that change the purchasable option. Note which control changes colour, which changes size and which changes model or package. A single combined dropdown may contain several of these dimensions in the same label.

Imagine two options both translate as “black regular.” One seller label ends in A and the other in B. Their thumbnails differ only in a seam under the pocket. Do not decide that one of the labels is redundant simply because the translated words are identical. Record the full original text, suffix and thumbnail for each. Your immediate goal is to identify what differs between them. Once that difference is known, the translation can be useful again without being asked to carry all of the product identity.
Change one control at a time

Select the first style while keeping other controls fixed. Record the main image, unit price, available sizes and any model code. Switch to the second style and repeat. If the size resets or becomes unavailable, note it. A size offered in one style does not necessarily remain selectable in another. When a seller uses separate colour and finish controls, avoid changing both in the same step; otherwise you will not know which control changed the picture or price.

If the photo changes from a jacket with a plain hood to one with a contrasting hood, that provides a promising lead. Check whether the text, detail gallery or seller description confirms the association. Some listings reuse a single gallery for every option. Conversely, a changed price may indicate a difference in included pieces rather than material quality. Treat each changed element as evidence about a specific property, not as conclusive proof of all the other properties you hope the version includes.
Preserve identifiers that translation can damage

Save codes, count indicators, measurements and punctuation exactly as presented where they distinguish versions. A model suffix, “2 pcs,” a fabric weight or a seller-specific colour number can be more informative than the translated adjective beside it. Preserve the original order of those details. Two labels can contain the same words and numbers in different combinations. Transforming them into a general description may remove the distinction you were trying to verify.

For instance, “model A, black, two pieces” describes something different from “model B, black, single piece” even though a clipped mobile selector may show only “black.” Expand the selector or open the original marketplace page if available. Take a screenshot that includes the listing context and the complete selected option. A standalone picture of a black swatch cannot identify which of the two bundles you mean. Keep your own readable explanation beside the original text, rather than replacing the original with your preferred translation.
Check whether apparent size words mean fit or product type

Words such as regular, large and short can describe garment length, bag capacity, frame size or seller-defined model names. A “large” accessory may be physically larger than another version while using the same strap length. A “short” jacket can refer to body length rather than sleeve length. Find the diagram or measurements attached to the selected option. If two versions share a chart, look for a model column or separate headings that identify which rows apply.

Use a hypothetical storage bag as an example. The large black option might be a single large bag, while black set might include two smaller bags. If you need to fit a specific object, the word large is insufficient. Compare opening size, interior dimensions and the count included. An order note such as “large please” could be misread if the seller uses a separate type named Large Set. Combining the original version code with the one deciding measurement supports a much more reliable selection.
Write a note that another person can act on

A useful purchase note identifies the listing, exact original option, required quantity and what should happen if it is unavailable. Adding a concise description can resolve ambiguity: “version B, second dark swatch, single jacket with contrast hood.” If the seller changes the order of the swatches after you save the note, the code and construction description remain helpful. Avoid relying on position alone. Also avoid authorizing a substitution by using broad wording such as “anything similar is fine” unless you truly accept the possible differences.

If several units are involved, list each option separately. For example, specify one model A in medium and two model B in large. Keep the total number of units as a cross-check, but do not let it replace the distribution. Three correct units in the wrong size mix still leave an incorrect order. When the order confirmation appears, compare every line with the note and check the price after selection. Resolve a discrepancy before treating the purchase as settled.
Use the account record to review the warehouse pictures

The developer describes iTaoBuy as an agent that can process marketplace links and provide warehouse QC photographs. When your particular unit arrives, connect the warehouse entry to the corresponding order line. Compare the visible model features with the decision you recorded. A correct-looking black colour does not answer whether the piece is lined, includes the hood option or came with the second accessory. Select the one view that would resolve the remaining uncertainty and ask whether that view is available.

For a finish that looks similar under warehouse lighting, a readable option label may be more useful than another distant photograph. For a lining discrepancy, an inside view can show something the label does not. Match the evidence to the property under review. If the unit appears wrong, send the original option and the corresponding visible feature together. Support can then compare what was ordered with what was received, rather than translating an isolated colour word and guessing why you are concerned.
Save a record that survives later listing edits

After the choice is verified, retain the original marketplace identifier, selected option, purchase confirmation and one identifying image of the actual unit. This is a compact archive that remains understandable even if the seller reorganizes the page or the agent changes a translated heading. If you reorder later, recheck availability and the current wording instead of assuming the old swatch position still represents the same product. Listings can change while keeping a familiar cover photograph.

The final question is practical: could another person reproduce your intended selection using the information you saved? If they would have to choose between two identical translations with no further clues, the record is incomplete. If they can locate the listing, select the correct model, colour and size, verify the number of pieces and recognize the feature that distinguishes it, the translation has served its purpose. You have converted a vague label into a purchase specification you can actually check.

If two colours share a code prefix, keep the entire suffix in your order note. In an illustrative listing, one option might end in 04A and a second in 04B. A note that records only 04 loses the distinguishing character even when the rest of the description looks accurate. Copy the codes from the original option menu and compare them with the selected entry in the cart. This extra check takes on particular importance when the translated colour names are identical.
Writing a precise iTaoBuy order note for a two-tone colourway

“Black and white, please” can describe two opposite designs. Turn a reference picture into an order instruction that identifies the seller option, the position of each colour and the change you would actually authorize.
Identify the selection the seller can fulfil

Start by opening the exact seller listing. A reference photograph gives a buying agent something to compare, but the available options describe what the seller can actually supply. Identify the marketplace, item number, seller and original option label. If the desired version appears in a gallery but never appears in the selector, treat availability as a question. A seller may keep old product pictures after a version has sold out, or use a group photograph for a listing that offers only some of the pictured designs.

Consider a track jacket with a pale body, black sleeves and a narrow stripe across the chest. A different option reverses the body and sleeve colours. Both may be translated as “black white.” Your note needs to identify the one option and the visible properties that distinguish it. Record the original text, style code and selected thumbnail, then add your own description. The code is useful if the image changes; the description is useful if the code has been translated or clipped.
Name the parts of the design consistently

Describe the product as a small set of named regions. For the jacket, use body, left sleeve, right sleeve, collar, cuff and stripe as needed. For shoes, use upper, sole, heel and accents. For a bag, distinguish body, base, handles and hardware. Avoid inventing elaborate terms that somebody looking at the item would struggle to recognize. The aim is to reduce ambiguity, not to produce a complete catalogue of every visible colour.

Pick a viewpoint when left and right matter. “Wearer's left” and “left side of the photograph” point to opposite sides in a typical front-facing picture. If the distinction matters, write which one you mean or describe a nearby fixed feature such as a pocket or zip. For the track jacket, “pale front body with black sleeves on both sides” may be sufficient.
